High-Rise Condominium Management in Chicago.

High-rises are operating systems, not just collections of units. CenterPoint coordinates the people, equipment, finances, and board decisions that keep complex Chicago condominium buildings dependable.

One accountable management system for a complex building.

Chicago high-rise boards must manage interdependent mechanical systems, employees and contractors, inspections, resident traffic, major projects, and substantial operating and reserve budgets. Our role is to put each responsibility on a visible calendar, assign ownership, document decisions, and give the board an accurate view of what requires attention next.

Building systems

Preventive schedules and vendor coordination for elevators, boilers, pumps, fire and life-safety systems, roofs, façades, garages, and domestic-water infrastructure.

On-site teams

Clear scopes, supervision, schedules, and escalation paths for door staff, engineers, janitorial teams, and association employees.

Capital planning

Multi-year planning that connects reserve studies, condition reports, competitive bids, owner communication, and board approvals.

24/7 response

A live emergency line, qualified dispatch, incident documentation, and next-business-day reporting to the board.

Financial controls

Resident operations

Move coordination, contractor access, amenity rules, service requests, notices, and consistent enforcement for dense communities.

Management the board can inspect.

  • Dedicated community association manager who knows the building
  • Annual operating calendar for inspections, renewals, and preventive work
  • Competitive bidding and documented board approvals
  • No separate capital-project planning or management-oversight fee
  • Illinois condominium-governance and Chicago building requirements
  • Board and resident portals with accessible records and work-order tracking

Changing managers without disrupting building operations.

A high-rise transition cannot depend on a folder handoff. CenterPoint builds a transition register covering bank access, contracts, insurance, employee records, open violations, inspection dates, keys and access systems, resident balances, active projects, litigation coordination, and emergency vendors. Responsibilities are tracked through the first 90 days so nothing critical disappears between management companies.

Boards receive a management scope tailored to the building’s staffing, amenities, equipment, and financial complexity. Pricing is a transparent flat monthly fee starting at $20 per unit, not a percentage of the association budget.

What high-rise boards should confirm before changing managers.

Clear scope, clear pricing, and a transition plan your board can evaluate before making a decision.

What makes high-rise condominium management different?

High-rises require one operating system for building equipment, inspections, employees and contractors, access and moves, resident communication, emergency response, large budgets, reserves, and capital projects. Each responsibility needs an owner, deadline, record, and escalation path.

Can CenterPoint coordinate on-site building staff and specialized vendors?

Yes. The management scope can include schedules, responsibilities, documentation, and escalation paths for door staff, engineers, janitorial teams, association employees, and specialized elevator, boiler, life-safety, façade, garage, and water-system vendors.

How does 24/7 high-rise emergency response work?

A live emergency line receives urgent calls around the clock, coordinates qualified response, documents the incident, and reports the event to the board. Building-specific contacts and escalation procedures are established during onboarding.

How much does high-rise condominium management cost?

CenterPoint uses a customized flat monthly fee starting at $20 per unit. Staffing, amenities, mechanical systems, financial complexity, resident operations, meeting needs, and the final service scope determine the proposal.

How do you transition a high-rise without disrupting operations?

The transition register covers banking, contracts, insurance, employees, inspections, keys and access systems, owner balances, open violations, active projects, litigation coordination, emergency vendors, and resident communication, with responsibilities tracked through the first 90 days.
